Candidate final HLM Model 5 coefficients in Table 6 (PDF p. 7, printed p. 35): male students -2.543 (parenthesized effect size 0.31), completion of computer course 1.694 (0.21), log usage time for study -0.118 (0.01), log usage time for purposes other than study 0.071 (0.01), satisfaction level of students in classes using ICT 0.750 (0.09), each p < .001; major city 1.457 (0.18), achievement level 0.052 (0.01), number of PCs per student 2.364 (0.29), each p < .05. These are separate candidate tests, not assigned values. Table 6 labels parentheses as effect sizes; the discussion references Cohen d benchmarks, but no metric is imposed on the unselected target. Other Model 5 coefficients: medium size 0.183, large size 0.036, small and medium-sized city 0.304, PCs per teacher 0.355, teacher computer usage ratio 0.958, teacher satisfaction 0.235; no significance stars. Model 5 random-effect chi-square 1127.753, p < .001, is another distinct test. Methods section 2.1 gives final analysis subjects 11,767 students nested in 173 schools, after complete questionnaire responses and exclusion of schools with 15 or fewer respondents. This is candidate HLM sample information only: not assigned globally to an unidentified test. HGLM Table 7 instead prints boundary-specific samples: 4876 students/172 schools for below basic/basic, 7542/172 for basic/average, 5315/173 for average/excellent. These overlapping boundary samples must not be summed. No N derivation or metric conversion performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
